Claude ↔ Vercel access audit

Verified live on 2026-09-16 · prepared for Justin Massion

From this cloud environment, Claude's requests to api.vercel.com pass through an organization agent proxy that injects Vercel credentials — and those credentials work: fetching a single deployment's status by its dpl_ ID reaches Vercel and authenticates. Everything else — deploying, creating projects, listing anything, reading logs, managing domains, even identifying the account — is blocked by the organization's network egress policy before it reaches Vercel. To change that, a Claude.ai organization owner must widen the Vercel rule in Claude Tag settings; until then Claude cannot publish anything to a public Vercel URL from here.

4endpoints working (deployment status by ID)
8endpoints blocked by org network policy
1fix, and it needs an owner: widen the proxy rule

What's working — 4 read-only routes

Each returned a Vercel-origin not_found JSON for a placeholder ID. A response from Vercel itself (not the proxy) proves the route is allowed and the injected token authenticates — an unauthenticated request would get 403 forbidden from Vercel, not not_found.

GET /v13/deployments/dpl_placeholder000000000000HTTP 404 · reached Vercel

Read one deployment's status by ID (v13)

Observed: {"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"Deployment not found"}}

GET /v8/deployments/dpl_placeholder000000000000HTTP 404 · reached Vercel

Read one deployment's status by ID (v8)

Observed: {"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"Deployment not found"}}

GET /v6/deployments/dpl_placeholder000000000000HTTP 404 · reached Vercel

Read one deployment's status by ID (v6)

Observed: {"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"Deployment not found"}}

What's not working — blocked by org network policy

Each returned HTTP 403 with request blocked: no rule allows… from the agent proxy. These requests never reached Vercel; the token's actual permissions there are untested for these routes.

GET /v2/userHTTP 403 · blocked by proxy

Identify the authenticated account (who am I)

Observed: request blocked: no rule allows host "api.vercel.com" — "Vercel" allows the host but not path "/v2/user" (allowed: "/v13/deployments/dpl_", "/v3/deployments/dpl_", "/v6/deployments/dpl_", "/v8/deployments/dpl_")

What it would have enabled: Identify which Vercel account or team the injected token belongs to.

What it would have enabled: Read a deployment's build and runtime logs to debug a failed deploy.

Practical consequence

In plain words: give Claude a deployment ID like dpl_abc123 and it can tell you whether that deployment is READY, ERROR, or still building. That is the whole capability. Claude cannot deploy a site, create a project, list projects or deployments, read build logs, manage domains, or even see which Vercel account the token belongs to. Therefore it cannot publish deliverables to a public Vercel URL today — the deploy endpoint itself is blocked.

What needs fixing / owner action

  1. A Claude.ai organization owner widens the Vercel rule in Claude Tag settings (claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag) to also allow: POST /v13/deployments, GET /v9/projects, POST /v10/projects, GET /v6/deployments, GET /v2/user, and GET /v2/deployments/*/events.
  2. Confirm the injected token's scope covers the target team — the blocked routes never reached Vercel, so the token's project-creation and deploy permissions there are unverified.
  3. Once both hold, Claude can deploy static HTML deliverables from this environment and verify the resulting public URLs end to end.

Alternative path: GitHub Pages on an imagine-os empty repository can host the same static deliverables — but creating a public site there also needs an owner's approval before Claude proceeds.

About the screenshots

These are terminal captures of the actual requests and responses, because Vercel's dashboard is not reachable with API-only access from this environment.

Agent proxy status: enabled on port 38087, non-selective (all HTTPS egress routed through it), no recent relay failures. The proxy status endpoint does not list per-service rules; the Vercel rule's allowed path prefixes above are quoted verbatim from its 403 responses.
